intent: Add a persistent conversational orchestrator session, separate from the user's interactive chat, for the OpenCode client. The user opens or attaches a second native session and types into it directly. At start the orchestrator receives an assigned scope (goal statement, baseline revision, compiled contracts) and does not inherit chat history; its lifespan is bounded to that scope. Within the scope it holds workflow authority: it may run route_task, compile tickets, and verify evidence through MCP or the shared CLI, but it never edits source directly. All execution is delegated to the existing per-task role workers (architect/engineer/reviewer) through scripts/roles.py, with receipts under .harness/roles as today, and workers complete their task directly without spawning further sessions. The orchestrator's scope is bound to its own worktree and paths so it cannot collide with concurrently running sessions. The user's own client session stops being the de facto orchestrator.

requirements.ORCH-SESSION-SEPARATION: The orchestrator runs as its own native OpenCode session with a stable recorded identity, distinct from and not inheriting history from the user's interactive chat; it is resumable across turns for the lifetime of its assigned scope.
requirements.ORCH-SCOPED-CONTEXT: The orchestrator receives its assigned scope (goal statement, baseline revision, compiled contract references) at start; its lifespan ends when the user closes the session or the scope's tickets close.
requirements.ORCH-WORKFLOW-AUTHORITY: The orchestrator may run route_task, compile tickets and verify evidence via MCP or the shared CLI, but never edits source directly; all source edits go through the bounded engineer path.
requirements.ORCH-DELEGATION: All execution is delegated through the existing per-task role launcher with receipts under .harness/roles; workers complete their assigned task directly without spawning further agent sessions.
requirements.ORCH-PARALLEL-SAFETY: The orchestrator's scope is bound to its own worktree and paths so it cannot collide with other concurrently running sessions.
requirements.ORCH-OPENCODE-V1: The first version targets OpenCode only, through the existing adapter pattern; other clients are not blocked but are out of scope for this ticket.
